bug_semantics: Any authenticated user can send GET /api/chat/users?q=%% (URL-encoded as %25%25) or q=__ and bypass the intended display-name substring filter. Database::escape() neutralizes SQL string syntax but leaves SQL LIKE metacharacters active; the query embeds the escaped input between '%' characters without an ESCAPE clause, so '%' and '_' match arbitrary active users and disclose their user IDs and display names (up to the query limit).
flaw_origin: Commit a7275859a5d6bc19c20827fe1ec6f6d925ea6f27 first added both the authenticated chat-user-search controller action and Chat::searchUsers(). Its new SQL used ud.display_name LIKE '%%%s%%' with only Database::escape($searchTerm), omitting LIKE-metacharacter escaping. Later commit 1dd0432a900d85f712b26c6be07dd5f70511d868 lowercased the term and moved SQL escaping into $escapedTerm but preserved the wildcard flaw; f9a180ba8de7ca7c6742be9b3f7a32028b7c9a6b removed email from the result but also preserved enumeration of IDs/display names. Thus a7275859a5d6bc19c20827fe1ec6f6d925ea6f27, not either later edit, is the smallest reachable-history BIC.
ai_marker: Absent. `git cat-file commit a7275859a5d6bc19c20827fe1ec6f6d925ea6f27` shows author and committer Thorsten Rinne <thorsten@phpmyfaq.de> and only the message `feat(chat): added basic classes, controllers and database (#3722)`; there are no Co-Authored-By, Generated-with, AI-tool, or bot-identity markers in the BIC commit object.
evidence: Advisory GHSA-6pvm-2vjj-rx4w / CVE-2026-47132 identifies the authenticated GET /api/chat/users?q=... path, the unescaped '%'/'_' LIKE semantics, affected range <4.2.0-alpha, first patched version 4.2.0-alpha, and fix bd4b08b012234ccfcff07bfe6518062475b29e0a. In the validated clone: (1) `git log --all --follow -S'function searchUsers' -- phpmyfaq/src/phpMyFAQ/Chat.php` returns only a7275859a5d6bc19c20827fe1ec6f6d925ea6f27 as the method's addition; `git log --all -S"LIKE '%%%s%%'" -- phpmyfaq/src/phpMyFAQ/Chat.php` independently returns that same first writer. (2) `git show a7275859a5d6bc19c20827fe1ec6f6d925ea6f27 -- phpmyfaq/src/phpMyFAQ/Chat.php phpmyfaq/src/phpMyFAQ/Controller/Frontend/Api/ChatController.php` shows the new authenticated route and new vulnerable LIKE query together. (3) `git ls-tree -r --name-only 0f8fd0a87b8bc75dcdbae9f093d5040344af896b -- phpmyfaq/src/phpMyFAQ/Chat.php phpmyfaq/src/phpMyFAQ/Controller/Frontend/Api/ChatController.php` produces no output, directly proving both files and therefore this flaw are absent from the immediate parent. (4) `git log -L 297,315:phpmyfaq/src/phpMyFAQ/Chat.php bd4b08b012234ccfcff07bfe6518062475b29e0a^` shows the a7275859 origin plus the non-curing edits 1dd0432a900d85f712b26c6be07dd5f70511d868 and f9a180ba8de7ca7c6742be9b3f7a32028b7c9a6b; `git blame -L 297,315 bd4b08b012234ccfcff07bfe6518062475b29e0a^ -- phpmyfaq/src/phpMyFAQ/Chat.php` corroborates those origins. (5) `git show bd4b08b012234ccfcff07bfe6518062475b29e0a` shows the direct fix: escape '|', '%', and '_' to '||', '|%', and '|_', add `ESCAPE '|'`, and add wildcard-literal regression coverage; `git log --all -S"str_replace(['|', '%', '_'], ['||', '|%', '|_']" -- phpmyfaq/src/phpMyFAQ/Chat.php` finds bd4b08b012234ccfcff07bfe6518062475b29e0a as the remediation's origin. (6) Tag containment gives the concrete boundaries: a7275859 is first present in 4.0/4.1/development-nightly-2026-01-20 (tag target 3de48e2dbdf96e5b6d6373a293fc606f4509cb63, whose parent is the BIC), while the 2026-01-19 nightlies predate it; bd4b08b is absent from the 2026-05-17 nightlies and first present in the 2026-05-18 nightlies. `git show --no-patch 4.2.0-alpha` resolves the formal first-patched tag to a429fb81a4efe1f7c0aeec5b7bf8a98a50509b85, a descendant containing bd4b08b, matching the advisory's first-patched boundary. (7) `git cat-file commit a7275859a5d6bc19c20827fe1ec6f6d925ea6f27` is the sole source used for AI attribution and contains only the human author/committer and plain issue-referencing subject quoted in ai_marker.
reasoning: The root cause is failure to distinguish SQL string escaping from LIKE-pattern escaping. The first commit that creates that exact data flow is a7275859: an authenticated request parameter reaches a LIKE pattern after only Database::escape(), and its parent has neither the sink class nor the route. Subsequent search refactors retain the same pattern semantics, so they are not BICs. bd4b08b directly closes the mechanism by escaping the pattern metacharacters and declaring the escape character, and the formal 4.2.0-alpha tag contains that fix. The BIC is an ordinary one-parent source commit, not a move/revert/release/backport or a merge object requiring decomposition. Because its raw commit object attributes both authoring roles to a human and carries no qualifying AI trailer or bot identity, the protocol requires NOT_AI regardless of any information outside that commit object.
